newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - May 30.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - May 30.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - Prices skidded through Thursday on growing speculation that strong production is overwhelming healthy demand, at least for the time being, Random Lengths said in its weekly lumber market review. Some traders said a dearth of orders from Japan diverted supplies into the domestic market.
The poular notion that thin stocks will force buyers' hand came under fire from traders who argued that there was ample wood in the pipeline to supply dealers' just-in-time needs.
The end of the month gave buyers an excuse to stand back and look for bargains, the lumber reporting agency said.

Mills lowered prices gradually in hopes of a pickup after their month-end sales push, but they routinely had to take counters to keep wood moving. The market's six-week retreat brought the Framing Composite Index within $4 of its 1997 low, which was registered January 3. When wholesalers speculated at all, it was on the short side of the market, the agency said.

Most secondaries traded back-to-back, countering mills hard to meet their customers' price targets. Treaters reported good sales to home centers restocking after the Memorial Day weekend. But prices on treated items slipped in line with bright stock.

Labor negotiations were under way in British Columbia amid talk that bargaining will be tough. Traders took a wait-and-see attitude. Reminders from some Canadian mills that they werte marking the end of the first quarter of Quota Year 2 also left buyers unimpressed. Tight supplies of trucks and railcars delayed shipments in many parts of the South, but the balance remained tipped in favor of buyers, Random Lengths said.
Boards largely bucked the trend in studs and dimension, but sales fell off. Supplies of Ponderosa shop increased, it said.
